description: Master rotation-agnostic heuristics for elite Pokemon TCG play, with stable IDs referenced by deck docs. Confidence: V=verified, S=sourced, T=theory/synthesis.

phases.deckbuilding: Deck construction: ratios, engines, line-building, card selection, archetype.
phases.pregame: Metagaming and tournament preparation before the event.
phases.opening: Mulligan, turn-order choice, and turn-1 setup.
phases.sequencing: Order of plays within a turn.
phases.prize_trade: The prize-trade and prize-mapping framework — the core scoring loop.
phases.resources: Board management, target selection, and resource/tempo management.
phases.mental: Mental game, practice methodology, and tournament management.

core: Pokemon TCG is a race to six prizes governed by the prize trade; deckbuilding and play serve (a) winning that exchange and (b) being consistent enough to execute the plan every game.

meta_heuristics.title: Consistency first
meta_heuristics.principle: Every slot competes against 'more engine.' Cut anything a dual-purpose card replaces; do not tech away the matchups you will actually face.

meta_heuristics.title: Math over vibes
meta_heuristics.principle: Mulligan odds, copy-count probability, and prize math are fixed across rotations — anchor decisions to them.

meta_heuristics.title: Prizes are the only score
meta_heuristics.principle: Damage, tempo, and disruption matter only insofar as they move the prize trade.

meta_heuristics.title: Information last, commitment last
meta_heuristics.principle: Sequence every turn from reversible to irreversible; deny the opponent reads.

meta_heuristics.title: Control the controllables
meta_heuristics.principle: Predict the field, prepare the lines, accept the variance.

heuristics.title: Baseline skeleton
heuristics.principle: Start from ~20 Pokemon / ~30 Trainer / ~10-11 Energy, tune +/-3.
heuristics.rationale: Balances board presence, engine, and attack cost; a testing starting point, not a law.

heuristics.title: Trainer budget
heuristics.principle: Inside ~30 Trainers: 6-12 Supporters (4-9 draw, 2-4 gust), 15-20 Items (8-10 search, 2-3 Stadiums).
heuristics.rationale: Draw+search is the engine; gust converts board control into prizes. Under-supporting draw causes bricking.

heuristics.title: Energy count
heuristics.principle: Default ~11 Energy; cut toward 8 as search density rises.
heuristics.rationale: Search fetches energy on demand, so high search density needs fewer raw copies. Decide count after building the engine.

heuristics.title: Basic floor
heuristics.principle: Run enough Basics to keep mulligans low — commonly ~10+.
heuristics.rationale: P(no Basic in 7) falls ~88%@1 -> ~53%@5 -> ~26%@10 -> ~5%@20. Each mulligan gives the opponent a card and info.

heuristics.title: Line scaling
heuristics.principle: Scale evolution counts by stage: 4 Basic attacker; 4-3 Stage 1; 4-2-4 Stage 2.
heuristics.rationale: The bottleneck is always the bottom of the line — you cannot evolve what you did not open.

heuristics.title: Rare Candy skip
heuristics.principle: In Stage 2 decks run 3-4 Rare Candy and thin/omit the Stage 1.
heuristics.rationale: Skip-the-middle buys a turn of tempo and frees deck slots; the Stage 1 becomes a backup line.

heuristics.title: Copy probability
heuristics.principle: Value each copy by draw probability, not feel.
heuristics.rationale: A 1-of appears in the opening 7 ~11.7%; a 4-of ~40%. 1->2 copies is the biggest per-slot consistency jump. Reserve 1-ofs for searchable cards.

heuristics.title: Engine type
heuristics.principle: Pick engine by need: exact-search for a few specific pieces (enables thin 1-of lines); pure-draw when you need multiple pieces per turn.
heuristics.rationale: Search maximizes precision; draw maximizes volume. Match the tool to the problem.

heuristics.title: Keep an engine
heuristics.principle: Run at least one dedicated consistency engine unless testing proves otherwise.
heuristics.rationale: Its real job is to rescue brick hands and smooth variance.

heuristics.title: Max core supporters
heuristics.principle: Near-max the Supporters that ARE your engine (3-4 copies of core setup/search Supporters).
heuristics.rationale: Load-bearing turn-1 cards must be hit on schedule.

heuristics.title: Consolidate
heuristics.principle: Cut any card whose job a dual-purpose card can also do.
heuristics.rationale: Slot efficiency is how a full engine + attackers + tech fit in 60. Ask: does one card do the work of two?

heuristics.title: Secondary roles
heuristics.principle: Build secondary attackers for a specific role: single-prize trade-fixer, fast revenge/carry, alternate-weakness, or a different weakness than the main.
heuristics.rationale: Each secondary should answer a problem the main attacker cannot.

heuristics.title: Tech for the field
heuristics.principle: Tech for the predicted field, not every possibility.
heuristics.rationale: Tech slots come out of consistency; dedicate them only to the top expected decks.

heuristics.title: Know your archetype
heuristics.principle: Know which strategy you execute — Aggression/Control/Mill/Stall — each is a stance on the prize trade.
heuristics.rationale: Your archetype dictates the default line in every ambiguous spot.

heuristics.title: Define win condition
heuristics.principle: Define your deck's win condition explicitly and build toward it.
heuristics.rationale: It tells you which resources to protect and which to spend freely.

heuristics.title: Predict the field
heuristics.principle: Predict the field before picking a deck — top 3-5 archetypes and rough share.
heuristics.rationale: Even a powerful deck loses to a field of counters; predict via results aggregators.

heuristics.title: Matchup spread
heuristics.principle: Choose for matchup spread, not one great pairing.
heuristics.rationale: ~50/50 across the whole field beats crushing one archetype and folding to another.

heuristics.title: Budget for rogue
heuristics.principle: Reserve ~10% of your forecast for rogue/'other'.
heuristics.rationale: The field is never fully predictable; budgeting for surprise prevents an auto-loss.

heuristics.title: Two counter layers
heuristics.principle: Stop at two layers of counter-picking.
heuristics.rationale: Countering the counter-of-the-counter loops back to vulnerability to the original decks.

heuristics.title: Local read
heuristics.principle: For local events factor in who is attending.
heuristics.rationale: Known pilots and pet decks let you make surgical tech choices.

heuristics.title: Test your read
heuristics.principle: Pressure-test your meta read with skilled peers.
heuristics.rationale: Collaborative forecasting catches blind spots a solo analysis misses.

heuristics.title: Turn-order choice
heuristics.principle: Going first vs second is deck-dependent: first = setup turn (no T1 attack); second = extra card + first attack.
heuristics.rationale: Setup-heavy decks want first; fast/aggressive decks want second. Decide by whose tempo plan needs the turn more.

heuristics.title: Turn-1 priority
heuristics.principle: Turn-1 priority: establish attacker-Basic -> develop engine -> build needed bench -> commit energy last.
heuristics.rationale: You cannot win a game you cannot start; T1 guarantees reaching the payoff.

heuristics.title: Buy optionality first
heuristics.principle: Going first, buy future optionality, not present tempo.
heuristics.rationale: With no attack available, maximize the number of strong plays available next turn.

heuristics.title: Draw then search
heuristics.principle: Draw before you search; search before you commit.
heuristics.rationale: Decide with full hand knowledge, then search only for what is left.

heuristics.title: Abilities after draw
heuristics.principle: Use board/choice Abilities after drawing, not before.
heuristics.rationale: Every irreversible decision should be made with the most information available that turn.

heuristics.title: Attach energy last
heuristics.principle: Attach energy as one of your last actions before declaring an attack.
heuristics.rationale: It is irreversible and telegraphs your plan; delaying preserves flexibility.

heuristics.title: Delay benching
heuristics.principle: Delay benching and other commitments until forced.
heuristics.rationale: Every benched Pokemon is a future target and a piece of the opponent's prize map.

heuristics.title: Reversible first
heuristics.principle: Master rule: reversible & info-gathering plays first, irreversible plays last.
heuristics.rationale: Order every turn from least-committal to most-committal.

heuristics.title: Break rules knowingly
heuristics.principle: Know when to break sequencing rules (e.g., desperate for a Basic -> search early, hold draw as backup).
heuristics.rationale: Heuristics are defaults, not handcuffs; information gain can justify reordering.

heuristics.title: Win the trade
heuristics.principle: Win by taking more prizes per KO than you concede.
heuristics.rationale: Most games are decided in the prize exchange, not raw damage. The central framework.

heuristics.title: Prefer single-prize
heuristics.principle: Prefer single-prize attackers when their damage is competitive.
heuristics.rationale: A 1-prize attacker doing 160 is strictly superior to a 2-prize one doing 160 for similar cost.

heuristics.title: Main attacker bars
heuristics.principle: A main attacker must be (a) fast and (b) deal enough damage relative to prizes surrendered.
heuristics.rationale: The more prizes it gives up when KO'd, the more damage it must produce to be worth running.

heuristics.title: Map the KO sequence
heuristics.principle: Map your full knockout sequence the moment you see the opponent's board.
heuristics.rationale: A clean 2-2-2 map beats a mixed 1-1-2-2; knowing the path tells you which attacker to use now.

heuristics.title: Target multi-prize
heuristics.principle: Target multi-prize Pokemon; do not waste gust/removal on 1-prize support.
heuristics.rationale: Prizes are the currency; spending resources on a 1-prize body is a losing exchange unless it enables their engine.

heuristics.title: Force inefficient maps
heuristics.principle: Force the opponent into an inefficient prize map (present 1-prizers so they need 6+ KOs).
heuristics.rationale: Asymmetric prize counts double the time you have to win.

heuristics.title: Limit bench liability
heuristics.principle: Do not bench multi-prize Pokemon you do not need this turn.
heuristics.rationale: An idle 2-prize Pokemon is two free prizes for a gust effect.

heuristics.title: Prize-check
heuristics.principle: Prize-check on every search; re-plan around prized key cards.
heuristics.rationale: Do not build a line that depends on a card sitting in the prizes.

heuristics.title: Fast-prizing cost
heuristics.principle: The cost of fast prizing scales with the format's disruption.
heuristics.rationale: Weak comeback/hand-refresh tools make racing low-risk; do not blanket-rule 'always set up fully first'.

heuristics.title: Spend at the right rate
heuristics.principle: Spend resources at the rate the matchup demands — no faster.
heuristics.rationale: Aggro mirrors are races (conserve); grind matchups reward out-attrition.

heuristics.title: Keep an out
heuristics.principle: Keep at least one path back to your engine in hand.
heuristics.rationale: Emptying your hand and bricking is the fastest way to lose from ahead.

heuristics.title: Play around outs
heuristics.principle: Play around the opponent's outs, not just their current board.
heuristics.rationale: Take the line that wins against the probable case while hedging the catastrophic one.

heuristics.title: Name tempo vs value
heuristics.principle: Trade tempo vs value deliberately — name which you are buying.
heuristics.rationale: Taking an immediate KO (tempo) vs building a stronger board (value) is the recurring decision.

heuristics.title: Track hidden info
heuristics.principle: Track your discard and deck as known information.
heuristics.rationale: Counting remaining copies converts guesses into odds.

heuristics.title: Protect setup in mirror
heuristics.principle: In the mirror, falling behind on tempo is hard to recover — protect your setup.
heuristics.rationale: Small early leads compound when both decks do the same thing.

heuristics.title: Mirror redundancy
heuristics.principle: In the mirror, run redundancy against single-point-of-failure plays.
heuristics.rationale: Do not let one snipe or disruption derail your whole plan.

heuristics.title: Differentiating tech
heuristics.principle: Differentiating tech, not raw power, often decides the mirror.
heuristics.rationale: The teched build wins the games the stock build draws.

heuristics.title: Lock is tempo
heuristics.principle: Treat lock/disruption as a tempo tool, not a permanent state.
heuristics.rationale: Apply and release situationally to maximize advantage windows.

heuristics.title: Decisions over results
heuristics.principle: Optimize for decision quality, not round results — the only controllable.
heuristics.rationale: Outcomes ride on variance you cannot touch; judge yourself on the correct line.

heuristics.title: Compartmentalize
heuristics.principle: Compartmentalize round-by-round.
heuristics.rationale: Projecting anxiety onto later rounds accumulates stress and degrades current decisions.

heuristics.title: Deliberate practice
heuristics.principle: Practice deliberately, not just frequently.
heuristics.rationale: Focused sessions with specific goals build skill; volume without intention plateaus.

heuristics.title: Review for mistakes
heuristics.principle: Review games for mistakes; post-game clarity proves in-game capability.
heuristics.rationale: If you can spot the error afterward, the gap is execution under pressure, not knowledge.

heuristics.title: Write a playbook
heuristics.principle: Write a per-matchup playbook before the event (lines, gameplan, prize map, techs, wincon).
heuristics.rationale: Documenting turns uncertainty into pre-made decisions executable on autopilot.

heuristics.title: Simulate conditions
heuristics.principle: Simulate tournament conditions in practice (timer, stakes, focus).
heuristics.rationale: Practicing under real conditions makes the event feel familiar.

heuristics.title: Physical baseline
heuristics.principle: Maintain the physical baseline — sleep 7+ hours, hydrate, eat.
heuristics.rationale: Physical state cascades directly into late-round decision quality.

heuristics.title: Confidence=competence
heuristics.principle: Interrupt automatic negative thoughts; align confidence with competence.
heuristics.rationale: Both under- and over-confidence cost games; build skill until belief matches ability.

heuristics.title: Copy systems
heuristics.principle: Study top players' systems, not their card lists.
heuristics.rationale: Replicating methods (testing, review, matchup study) compounds faster than copying a deck.
